title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo's autonomous vehicles were deployed into a traffic situation outside the conditions for which they were designed. During Fourth of July celebrations in San Francisco, unexpected road closures and extreme congestion left multiple vehicles stationary for extended periods until their batteries drained completely. The system lacked sufficient battery capacity or contingency protocols to handle a major disruption that deviated from normal operating patterns.

This represents a failure in operational resilience rather than a technical failure of the autonomous driving system itself. The vehicles functioned as programmed but could not manage the resource constraints imposed by an unusual event. Catching this would have required either larger battery capacity for extended idle periods, pre-positioned charging infrastructure in high-congestion zones, or a policy of not operating on days when major traffic disruptions are foreseeable.

One vehicle also caught fire after driving over fireworks on the street, which represents an external hazard. It is not established whether this was a failure of the vehicle's systems or solely the result of the fireworks themselves.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets during Fourth of July celebrations on Saturday after their batteries drained while stuck in heavy traffic. Video verified by NBC News showed at least a dozen stationary vehicles, many of them Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets following a fireworks display near the Golden Gate Bridge. The company attributed the incident to major traffic disruptions, high volumes of travelers, and unplanned road closures that created unexpected congestion. Waymo's roadside assistance team worked to clear the vehicles, and the company stated it is evaluating ways to improve resilience during major traffic disruptions.

One Waymo vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks that someone had set off on the street, though no injuries were reported. Residents complained about the situation, with one person noting they spent nearly two hours in standstill traffic. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office announced plans to have conversations with public and private partners about improving the experience for future events. This incident follows a previous December incident when Waymo vehicles stopped at intersections during a city power outage that affected more than 100,000 customers.
